items.title: 52145_Andrew Blakeney oral history interview
items.q: Interviewer mentions Coney as the son of W. B. Woodman, who played on the date with the interviewee. Interviewee does not mention Coney directly or describe a personal relationship.

ctx.x: Oh? We had him listed here as being a banjo player, but perhaps he was a piano. There were also other musicians on the date with you at the time, such as William Calhoun and W. B. Woodman, who was the father of Coney and Britt Woodman. Britt Woodman was a fine tromonist who played for many years with Duke Ellington, and who at this time I believe is active in New York.
Tell us a little bit about the lesser known musicians, maybe like William Calhoun. He was a multi-reed player, right?
